title: The Death of Karna (Days 16–17)
body:
The Death of Karna (Days 16–17)

कालः कलयतामहम् ॥

Translation: Among subduers, I am Time. (Bhagavad Gita 10.30)

Following Drona's demise, Karna was anointed the Supreme Commander of the Kuru forces, standing in his magnificent war-chariot with King Shalya serving as his reluctant, demoralizing charioteer. Over the course of two days, Karna displayed the peak of his legendary heroism. On the sixteenth day, Bhima finally extracted his terrifying, long-awaited revenge on Dushasana. Intercepting him in a violent duel, Bhima dragged him from his chariot, ripped open his chest, drank his blood to fulfill his sacred vow, and carried the blood in his palms to bind the dishevelled hair of Draupadi, washing away thirteen years of deep, burning humiliation.
On the seventeenth day, the long-awaited duel between the two supreme archers of the age, Arjuna and Karna, commenced. The heavens were filled with devas and rishis who gathered to witness this historic clash of cosmic forces. Karna invoked the fiery Sarpastra (Snake Arrow), wherein the spirit of Ashwasena—the serpent who had survived the burning of the Khandava forest—had entered. Directed at Arjuna's throat, the arrow flew like a streak of lightning. At the critical moment, Sree Krishna, with a swift downward pressure of His divine foot, sank Arjuna's chariot five inches into the mud. The blazing arrow missed Arjuna's throat, striking off his golden crown and turning it to black dust.
As the battle resumed, the relentless wheel of Karma caught up with the tragic hero. The left wheel of Karna's chariot suddenly sank deep into the blood-sodden mire, and simultaneously, the curses of his past began to bear their fatal fruit. He found himself unable to recall the invocatory mantras for the Brahmastra, which he had learned through deception from Sage Parasurama, and which the sage had cursed him to forget in his hour of greatest need.
Karna descended from his chariot, leaving his bow Vijaya behind, and desperately attempted to lift the wheel from the mud. He appealed to Arjuna's sense of Kshatriya chivalry, requesting a pause while he set his chariot right. Sree Krishna broke in with a devastating, righteous denunciation, demanding to know where Karna's chivalry had been when Draupadi was dragged into the assembly, when Yudhishthira was cheated at dice, and when six veterans united to slaughter the unarmed, isolated Abhimanyu. Silenced by the truth of Sree Krishna's words, Karna bowed his head in shame. Sree Krishna commanded Arjuna to strike the final blow before Karna could reclaim his weapons. Stifling his hesitation, Arjuna discharged a crescent-headed shaft that struck Karna's neck, and the mighty soul of the Sun-son departed, leaving his body like a fallen golden mountain on the field.
